_about: The single source of truth for what Fleet Radar watches.
Read by: the Bright Data collectors (which URLs to scrape), the classifier
(which packages to reason about), and the correlation engine (how to match a
radar package back to the package names the agent actually reports).
SOURCE PAGES ARE CONTENT PAGES, NOT INDEX PAGES. Schema v1 pointed at pages
like docs.djangoproject.com/en/stable/releases/ - which is a list of links,
not release notes. Those pages carry versions and dates but no changelog
prose, and changelog prose is the entire input to Type 1 detection. Every URL
below was fetched and confirmed to contain real breaking-change text.
CHANGELOG SOURCES ARE TEMPLATED PER RELEASE LINE. Release notes live at one
page per version, so a changelog source is a url_template plus the versions
to expand it over. All pages from one template share a structure, which is
exactly what `bdata scraper run <id> --urls a,b,c` batches over: one scraper
per template, run against every version of that template.
STRUCTURES ARE DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT across the five packages - Sphinx docs,
a vendor blog post, a vendor release-notes page, and a GitHub releases feed.
A scraper tuned to one cannot read another, so each template gets its own
collector, and self-healing is demonstrated per structure rather than once.

packages._why: Ships on every Linux host and has a strict, well-published support window.
packages._version_granularity_note: Support and EOL are tracked per 3.x line, so 3.7.0 and 3.7.9 share a verdict.

changelog.structure: Sphinx docs. Breaking changes live under 'Deprecated', 'Removed' and 'Porting to Python 3.x' sections.
changelog._volume_note: Largest source in the watchlist at ~115k chars per page. Bound extraction to the relevant sections rather than whole-page text.

eol.structure: Official status table: branch, status, first release, end of support.

packages._why: Best breaking-change signal in the watchlist - release notes carry an explicit, consistently titled backwards-incompatible section.

changelog.structure: Sphinx docs with a dedicated 'Backwards incompatible changes in X.Y' section - the cleanest Type 1 signal we have.

eol.structure: Supported-versions table plus an unsupported-versions list with end-of-life dates.

packages._why: Fixed LTS calendar makes EOL verdicts unambiguous and easy to defend on stage.
packages._version_granularity_note: Node support is tracked per major line (18.x, 20.x, 22.x).

changelog.structure: Vendor blog post. Breaking changes are the 'Semver-Major Commits' list - a prose feed, structurally unlike the docs pages.

eol.structure: Official release schedule table with end-of-life dates per major line.

packages._why: The highest-stakes package here - an unsupported OpenSSL is a real security exposure, which is the impact story.

changelog.structure: Vendor release-notes page. Smallest source (~9k chars) and the least consistently formatted.

eol.structure: Third-party aggregator; used because OpenSSL publishes no single official EOL table.

packages._why: npm breadth. Carries a changelog signal only - no formal EOL calendar exists, which is itself a realistic case the pipeline must tolerate.

changelog.structure: GitHub releases feed - all releases on one server-rendered page, so no template. Note GitHub *blob* pages lazy-load via JS and are unusable without JS rendering; *releases* pages render server-side.
changelog._no_template_note: The only changelog source that is a single page rather than one page per version.
